title: ClampFISH Protocol
author: Sara H Rouhanifard
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qeydtfw
materials: Aspirate media and rinse cells with 1X PBS.
Now you have the probe design software!
Use parafilm to seal the plate.
Aspirate wash buffer and replace with 2X SSC.
Aspirate click reaction and replace with wash buffer.

To complete the experiment, aspirate Wash buffer and replace with 2X SSC. Add DAPI to visualize nuclei on microscope. If using Cy5 for detection, mount slides with anti-fade buffer: a. 'Anti-Fade' buffer: 1mL volume 850 µL nuclease-free (NF) H 2 O 40 µL 10% glucose 100 µL 20X SSC 10 µL 1M Tris @ pH8 (this helps with oxidase proton products) We typically prepare a pre-mix containing water, SSC and Tris, as well as a stock of 10% glucose. We then combine the pre-mix with the glucose just before we add it to the sample. b. ----Glucose Oxidase Prep---- This is required to reduce photobleaching of Cy5 by dissolved oxygen. Glucose + Oxygen in sample --(GluOx)--> less O 2 in sample. Glucose oxidase stock enzyme is aliquoted out and frozen for storage. Note: Glucose oxidase tends to 'go bad' with repeated freeze/thaw cycles. In order to keep it working, aliquot it after the first thaw, so you’ll need to go through less than 5-10 freeze-thaws per aliquot. Materials needed: Glucose oxidase (Sigma, G2133-10KU), Catalase (Sigma, C3515-10MG) , 2X SSC, 10% Glucose. c. During 2nd wash, prepare 'Anti-Fade' buffer if there’s a Cy5-labelled probe. If not, you can proceed and image in 2xSSC. Add 40 µl of 10% glucose to 960 µl antifade-premix. Split anti-fade buffer into 100 & 900 µL volumes. 50 µL is for enzyme, 900 µL is for equilibrating sample. Vortex catalase in its amber vial from 4°C. Take out glucose oxidase from -20°C only when ready to add. Add 1 µL of oxidase enzyme and 1 µL of catalase to the 100 µL anti-fade buffer. Add 100 µL of glucose oxidase+catalase mix to sample. Use clean tweezers to add clean coverslip to squash & reduce O 2 .

steps.title: Grow cells to confluence
steps.instruction: Seed cells in multi‑well chamber slides and grow until they reach 50–70 % confluence, leaving space between cells for clean segmentation.

steps.title: Fix cells
steps.instruction: Aspirate PBS, add fixation solution, and incubate for 10 min (00:10:00).

steps.title: Rinse and ethanol fix
steps.instruction: Aspirate fixation solution, rinse cells three times with 1 X PBS, then aspirate the final PBS wash and add 70 % ethanol to each well. Samples may be stored in 70 % ethanol at 4 °C for long periods; ensure the ethanol level is topped up regularly.

steps.title: Obtain software license
steps.instruction: Request licensing permission at https://flintbox.com/public/project/50547/, then email arjunrajlab@gmail.com with your Bitbucket username to obtain access to the Raj lab probe‑design repository.

steps.title: Clone probe‑design code
steps.instruction: In a terminal, navigate to the desired directory and run the clone command shown by clicking “clone” on the repository page, e.g. hg clone https://srouhanifard@bitbucket.org/arjunrajlaboratory/probedesign.

steps.title: Add code to MATLAB path
steps.instruction: Add the cloned source code folder and all its subfolders (the “rajlab” directory) to the MATLAB path and click Save.

steps.title: Create target sequence file
steps.instruction: Open the UCSC Genome Browser (http://genome.ucsc.edu/cgi-bin/hgGateway), select the species, note the genome build (e.g., hg19, mm10), click the RefSeq gene, choose an isoform (if unsure, pick the isoform with the greatest common sequence among all isoforms), click the isoform track, select “Genomic Sequence…”, do NOT mask repeats, submit, copy the resulting FASTA entries into a plain‑text file named <targetname>.txt.

steps.title: Run probe design script
steps.instruction: In MATLAB, run findprobesHD('targetname.txt',20,'outfilename','targetname_30mer_target','species','mouse','oligolength',30,'allowableGibbsFE',[-50,-30],'targetGibbsFE',-40).

steps.title: Map and edit probe sequences
steps.instruction: Open the output file, map the new 30‑mer probe sequences onto your SnapGene file, and select probes that do not overlap existing smFISH probes (overlap is not critical).

steps.title: Add adapter sequences
steps.instruction: For each probe add the following adapters: PODXl_P1_left = /5Hexynyl/actttggtggctctgACATCATAGT; PODXl_P1_right = /5Phos/aagtgactgt tgttgatgttgtggc/3AzideN/. Order both left and right arms as 100 nmol DNA oligos; the right arm (3’ NHS‑azide) must be HPLC‑purified.

steps.title: Assemble probe reaction (no enzyme)
steps.instruction: Combine the following components (final concentrations indicated): 400 µM left arm, 400 µM left adapter, 400 µM right arm, 400 µM right adapter, 400 µM backbone, 2 X reaction buffer, and nuclease‑free H₂O to the desired volume.

steps.title: Add 5′ phosphate (optional)
steps.instruction: To phosphorylate left‑arm oligos enzymatically, mix 10 µl DNA (4 nmol), 35 µl 10 X buffer, 7 µl 80 mM ATP, 3.5 µl T4 PNK (10 U/µl), and water to 350 µl; incubate at 37 °C for 5.5 h, heat‑inactivate at 65 °C for 20 min, ethanol‑precipitate, and resuspend in 10 µl to obtain a 400 µM stock.

steps.title: Add 3′ azide (optional)
steps.instruction: To azidate the right‑arm oligo, combine 5 µl 400 µM right arm (3′ OH), 5 µl 4 mM N6‑(6‑Azido)hexyl‑3′‑dATP, 4 µl TdT enzyme, 10 µl Transferase buffer, and 26 µl nuclease‑free H₂O; incubate 90 min at 37 °C, inactivate 10 min at 70 °C, purify with a Monarch column, and resuspend in 5 µl (~400 µM).

steps.title: Heat reaction components
steps.instruction: Heat the assembled reaction mixture to 70 °C for 3 min (00:03:00).

steps.title: Cool reaction components
steps.instruction: Allow the mixture to equilibrate at room temperature for 5 min (00:05:00).

steps.title: Add T7 DNA ligase
steps.instruction: Add 2 µl of T7 DNA ligase (pre‑diluted 1:10 in nuclease‑free H₂O) to the cooled reaction.

steps.title: Ligate probes
steps.instruction: Incubate the ligation mixture at room temperature in the dark for at least 1 h (overnight is acceptable) (01:00:00).

steps.title: Purify ligation product
steps.instruction: Purify the ligation reaction using the Monarch PCR & DNA Cleanup Kit according to the manufacturer’s steps 42‑48. If the sample overloads a column, split it across multiple columns to improve yield.

steps.title: Elute into TE
steps.instruction: Add 80 µl TE buffer to the purified sample and mix.

steps.title: Bind to column
steps.instruction: Add 700 µl binding buffer to the sample, load onto a Monarch column, and let bind.

steps.title: Spin down column
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the column for 1 min (00:01:00).

steps.title: Wash column
steps.instruction: Wash the column twice with 200 µl Wash buffer, discarding the flow‑through after each wash.

steps.title: Elute purified probes
steps.instruction: Transfer the column to a new micro‑fuge tube, add 60 µl elution buffer to the center of the matrix, wait 1 min, then centrifuge to collect the eluate.

steps.title: Label chambers
steps.instruction: Label the top part of each chamber slide; the label will not be imaged.

steps.title: Prepare primary hybridization mix
steps.instruction: For each well, mix 50 µl clampFISH hybridization buffer with 0.5 µl of each clampFISH primary probe.

steps.title: Wash wells before hybridization
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl Wash buffer to each well of an 8‑well chamber slide, pipetting against the wall to avoid dislodging cells.

steps.title: Add primary hybridization mix
steps.instruction: Pipette 50 µl of the primary hybridization mix into the middle of each well.

steps.title: Cover and humidify
steps.instruction: Place a cover glass on top, gently pat down with forceps to remove bubbles, and humidify the chamber with a kimwipe soaked in Wash buffer.

steps.title: Incubate primary hybridization
steps.instruction: Incubate the slide at 37 °C for at least 4 h (overnight is acceptable) (04:00:00).

steps.title: Post‑hybridization wash and seal
steps.instruction: Remove the slide from the incubator, peel off parafilm, add Wash buffer (the buffer will seep under the cover glass and lift it), use tweezers to fully remove the cover slip, then reseal the plate with fresh parafilm.

steps.title: Post‑wash heat step
steps.instruction: Place the sealed plate at 37 °C for 20 min (00:20:00).

steps.title: Prepare secondary hybridization mix
steps.instruction: For each well, mix 50 µl clampFISH hybridization buffer with 1 µl of the appropriate clampFISH secondary probe (MM2 series). Use tertiary probes when applicable.

steps.title: Add secondary hybridization mix
steps.instruction: Pipette 50 µl of the secondary mix into the middle of each well, cover with a glass slip, pat down, and humidify as before.

steps.title: Incubate secondary hybridization
steps.instruction: Incubate at 37 °C for at least 2 h (02:00:00).

steps.title: Post‑secondary wash and seal
steps.instruction: Remove parafilm, add Wash buffer to lift the cover slip, remove the slip with tweezers, reseal with parafilm, and incubate at 37 °C for 20 min (00:20:00).

steps.title: Prepare click reaction mixture
steps.instruction: For each well make 250 µl of click solution: 3.75 µl 5 mM CuSO₄ (75 µM final), 1.875 µl 20 mM BTTAA (75 µM final), 6.25 µl 100 mM sodium ascorbate (150 µM final), add 2 X SSC/0.25 % Triton (volume to bring total to 250 µl), and bring to volume with nuclease‑free H₂O. Aspirate the existing 2 X SSC from the wells and replace with the click mixture.

steps.title: Click reaction incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the click mixture in the wells for 20 min at 37 °C.

steps.title: Repeat hybridization cycles
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 23‑34 (primary/secondary hybridizations, washes, click reaction) as needed, adding tertiary probes (P9 series) for each additional round until the desired amplification level is reached.

steps.title: Prepare smFISH detection mix
steps.instruction: Mix 1 µl of a 5 µM probe with 50 µl smFISH hybridization buffer (10 % formamide, 2 X SSC, 10 % dextran sulfate).

steps.title: Hybridize smFISH probe
steps.instruction: Aspirate Wash buffer from the wells, add the smFISH detection mix to the center of each well, place a cover glass on top, and incubate at 37 °C for at least 6 h (06:00:00).

steps.title: Final smFISH washes
steps.instruction: Wash each well twice with Wash buffer containing 10 % formamide and 2 X SSC, discarding the wash after each step.
